protocol.description:
This protocol allows a client to query and configure displays managed by the NVIDIA Display Config Server (DCS).
Warning: This protocol is unstable and subject to change without notice.

interface.name: zwp_dcs_manager
interface.description: This object is where the usage begins. The configuration tool will connect to the wayland socket and create a new manager object. This manager object is used to get the DCS companion object to a given wl_output advertised by the system. It is also used to create topology objects which are used for atomically updating the system state.

request.name: get_output

description.summary: create a zwp_dcs_output for a wl_output

request.description: Creates a zwp_dcs_output object which extends the provided wl_output.

request.name: create_topology
request.description: Creates a zwp_dcs_topology object which is used to atomically commit configuration changes across multiple displays.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroys the manager object. Objects created through it, such as zwp_dcs_output and zwp_dcs_topology, are not affected and remain valid.

interface.name: zwp_dcs_output
interface.description:
This object is used to describe the current physical display count and layout. It extends wl_output, meaning wayland global objects visible in wl_registry will be added and removed to reflect the current display state. Most of the display information comes from wl_output, however this allows us to attach display config server specific information to each output.
Note that the events here will be resent on any changes. Unlike wl_output's values which are sent once, these may be resent if there have been any changes.
Display connection and removal are reported through wl_registry: a newly connected display appears as a new wl_output global, and a display that is unplugged has its wl_output global removed with wl_registry.global_remove. A zwp_dcs_output follows the wl_output it extends. Once that global has been removed the server sends no further events on the zwp_dcs_output, and the client should destroy it along with the wl_output. Mode ids learned from it are no longer valid. A display that is plugged back in is a new wl_output global with a new zwp_dcs_output and freshly assigned mode ids; there is no identity carried across the unplug.
Because removal is asynchronous, a client may send a request naming a wl_output whose global has already been removed on the server. Such a request is not a protocol error. The server treats the output as one it does not manage: for a zwp_dcs_topology this surfaces at commit as an unknown_output error for that display, and the commit fails as a whole so the client can re-enumerate and decide what to do with the remaining displays.

event.name: mode
event.description:
Sends one supported mode for this output. The id is an opaque value chosen by the server that identifies this mode on this output for the lifetime of the zwp_dcs_output. Clients pass it back to zwp_dcs_topology.set_mode and match it against current_mode and preferred_mode. Ids carry no other meaning: they need not be contiguous, ordered, or comparable across outputs.
All mode events for an output are sent before current_mode, preferred_mode, and done.

event.name: current_mode
event.description: Identifies the mode currently set on this output, by the id given in a previous mode event. Sent after the mode list; may be resent on its own when the active mode changes.

event.name: preferred_mode
event.description: Identifies the display's preferred mode, by the id given in a previous mode event. Sent after the mode list.

event.name: device

description.summary: the DRM device for this output

event.description: The DRM device that drives this output. The array holds the dev_t of the device's primary node as an array of sizeof(dev_t) bytes in native byte order, the same encoding wp_linux_dmabuf_feedback uses for main_device.

event.name: number
event.description: The ID number (1-n) of the display.

event.name: done

description.summary: all DCS output state has been sent

event.description: Signals that all DCS output state has finished sending.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroys this object. The underlying wl_output is not affected, and mode ids learned from this object stay valid for use with zwp_dcs_topology.set_mode.

interface.name: zwp_dcs_topology
interface.description:
A topology stages configuration changes for any number of displays and commits them as one atomic update to the display wall. Requests that change display state take the wl_output of the display they apply to. Setting the same value twice for one output replaces the earlier value; nothing takes effect until commit.
Sub-protocols extend a topology with their own topology objects (for example zwp_dcs_quadro_sync_topology), which stage their state the same way and are applied by this object's commit.
The server will apply committed topologies one at a time in the order they are received. Topologies may be committed with disjoint sets of outputs and may be submitted in any order clients prefer, so long as the updates to the display(s) are valid and correct. If there is an issue with applying a specific configuration then eror events will be sent so the client may correct it and re-commit. On success, the done event is sent.

enum.name: error
enum.description: Reasons a display's staged state was rejected, sent with the error event.

entry.name: unknown_output
entry.summary: the wl_output is not a display managed by DCS

entry.name: invalid_mode
entry.summary: the mode id does not belong to this output

entry.name: invalid_state
entry.summary: the requested state for this display could not be validated or applied

request.name: set_mode

description.summary: stage a mode change for a display

request.description: Stages a mode change for the given display. The id comes from a zwp_dcs_output.mode event of the zwp_dcs_output created for this same wl_output. An id that does not belong to the output makes the commit fail with invalid_mode for this display.

arg.name: id
arg.summary: id of the mode to set

request.name: commit
request.description:
Commits every staged change in this topology and in the sub-protocol topology objects created from it. The server answers every commit with any number of error events, one per display that had a problem, any number of error events from sub-protocol topology objects, and then exactly one done event whose success argument says whether the commit was applied. done is always the last event of the reply. Commits are processed in order, so a client that waits for done before committing again can match each reply to its request.
If a display named by this topology is removed before the commit is processed, the commit fails with unknown_output for that display and nothing is applied, as described on zwp_dcs_output. The staged state for the other displays is kept, so the client may re-enumerate and commit again without the missing display. A display connected after a topology was created can be named by it normally.
A commit changes only the displays it names. Every other display keeps whatever state it had, whether that came from an earlier commit or from the server's own configuration. Any number of topologies may exist at once and their commits may name disjoint or overlapping sets of displays. The server applies commits one at a time in the order they arrive, for a display named by several commits the most recent commit will be the final state. Sub-protocols define how their own state behaves across commits, for example see zwp_dcs_quadro_sync_topology.
If the commit fails, nothing was applied and the topology stays alive with all of its staged state. The client can correct the offending display and commit again without rebuilding the topology.
If the commit succeeds, the commit is complete and the topology's lifetime is over. The client must destroy it, along with any sub-protocol topology objects created from it. The only request permitted on these objects after done is destroy.

event.name: done
event.description: Ends the reply to a commit. With success set, every staged change was validated and applied, the displays are in the requested state, and the topology is finished; see commit for what the client must do next. With success clear, nothing was applied and the topology stays alive so the client can correct it and commit again. Any error events explaining a failure were sent before this event; a failure with no error events means the problem was not specific to one display and the server logged the reason.

arg.name: success
arg.summary: 1 if the commit was applied, 0 if not

event.name: error
event.description: Names one display whose staged state was rejected and the reason. One event is sent per offending display, before the done event that ends the reply.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroys this topology. Any uncommitted state is discarded. This is the required final request after a commit reports done, and may also be sent at any other time to abandon the topology. Sub-protocol topology objects created from this topology are not destroyed, but since they can only be applied through this topology's commit the client should destroy them as well.
